scene.note: A search reads every row of a table, until an index lets it go straight to the rows it needs.

steps.note: The plan of Winnie's search for one day says it scans every visit.
Today every visit is read to find the few of that day.
With an index on the column the search looks up, it goes straight to that day's visits.
The plan now says SEARCH, and names your index.
Finding one owner's animals reads every animal.
An index on the column that points at the owner finds them directly, in a join too.
A vet's own visits from a date on: one part compared exactly, one a range.
One index holds both columns, in the order that keeps one vet's visits together, by date.
The plan shows the index used for both parts of the search.
The plan of each query the practice runs names the index it uses, if any.
Each index is changed on every change to its table, used or not.
The index that no plan names goes; the others stay.
